headline: Amazon Bedrock expands support for NVIDIA and OpenAI models in AWS GovCloud.

items.title: How Amazon Bedrock catches AI-generated phishing
items.summary: Amazon Bedrock has introduced a new system to detect AI-generated phishing emails, enhancing security for email systems. This sophisticated approach leverages AI to identify and mitigate phishing threats, which have become increasingly advanced, posing a significant risk to businesses. The system's ability to recognize patterns typical of AI-generated content helps security teams manage threats more effectively. This move underscores Bedrock's commitment to refining AI's role in cybersecurity.
items.why_it_matters: Tech leads should note the increased role of AI in cybersecurity, as it impacts how AI tools should be integrated into existing systems for enhanced protection.

items.title: Run NVIDIA Nemotron and OpenAI GPT OSS models on Amazon Bedrock in AWS GovCloud (US)
items.summary: Amazon Bedrock has expanded its support in AWS GovCloud (US) to include NVIDIA Nemotron models and OpenAI’s GPT OSS models. This release allows developers to access powerful models like NVIDIA's Nano 9B and Super 120B, as well as OpenAI's GPT OSS 120B and 20B models. These models offer enhanced capabilities for complex AI tasks, particularly for US-based projects requiring stringent compliance with government regulations. The integration facilitates seamless deployment and scaling of advanced AI projects within secure environments.
items.why_it_matters: This expansion provides tech leads with more robust model options for government-compliant AI projects, enhancing the capability and compliance of AI systems.

items.title: Simplify model selection in Amazon Bedrock with the open source Model Profiler
items.summary: Amazon has released the Model Profiler, an open-source tool designed to streamline model selection in Amazon Bedrock. It aggregates metadata from AWS APIs and external sources into a single searchable interface, allowing developers to easily compare and select models. This tool supports real-world scenarios and is deployable within individual AWS environments, making it easier to manage and utilize a broad range of models for various AI applications.

items.title: Accelerate protein design with BoltzGen on Amazon SageMaker AI
items.summary: BoltzGen, a tool for protein design, can now be deployed on Amazon SageMaker AI. The tool supports end-to-end protein design experiments, allowing for quick validation and production batch processing. It offers two execution modes for different stages of design, providing flexibility for researchers and developers working in biotechnology and pharmaceuticals.

items.title: PACE: A Neuro-Symbolic Framework for Plausible and Actionable Counterfactual Explanations
items.summary: The PACE framework aims to improve machine learning model interpretability by generating counterfactual explanations. These explanations highlight minimal changes needed to alter a model's decision, offering more plausible and actionable insights than traditional methods. This approach could significantly aid in debugging and refining AI models by providing clearer insights into decision boundaries and potential biases.

items.title: Auto-FL-Research: Agentic Search for Federated Learning Algorithms
items.summary: This research proposes a new method for optimizing federated learning (FL) algorithms. By focusing on consequential algorithmic choices like optimizer variants and server aggregation rules, the study aims to streamline FL processes and enhance performance. This framework could help developers more efficiently design and implement FL systems, reducing the cost and complexity of algorithm development.

items.title: Vercel's Andrew Qu on why agents are a new kind of software
items.summary: Andrew Qu, Vercel's Chief of Software, discusses the development of their agent framework, Eve, highlighting the importance of skills, sandboxes, and agent-readable websites. This perspective indicates a shift towards more autonomous and interactive software architectures that could redefine how developers approach AI integration and deployment.

all_items.title: Best practices for multi-turn reinforcement learning in Amazon SageMaker AI
all_items.summary: In this post, we share best practices for reliable multi-turn RL training. We cover how to build a training environment you can trust, set up an external evaluation, design a reward aligned with the end task, manage what changes once the agent runs for multiple turns, and monitor the metrics that tell you when to iterate.

all_items.title: Run NVIDIA Nemotron and OpenAI GPT OSS models on Amazon Bedrock in AWS GovCloud (US)
all_items.summary: We're excited to introduce US-based frontier open-weight models in AWS GovCloud (US). With this release, Amazon Bedrock now supports OpenAI’s open-weight GPT OSS models (120B and 20B) and NVIDIA Nemotron (Nano 9B v2, Nano 12B v2, Nano 30B, Super 120B) models. In this post, we cover these models and their capabilities, the inference options for data residency, the available service tiers and how to get started.

all_items.title: Building a serverless A2A gateway for agent discovery, routing, and access control
all_items.summary: In this post, you will learn how to build a serverless A2A gateway on AWS that hosts multiple agents behind a single domain using path-based routing (/agents/{agentId}). Standard A2A clients work without modification.

all_items.title: Structured memory filtering with metadata in AgentCore Memory
all_items.summary: In this post, you will learn how metadata works across configuration, ingestion, and retrieval, explore enterprise use cases including multi-agent and multi-tenant architectures, and discover best practices for implementation.

all_items.title: HippoRAG: Neurobiologically inspired RAG using Amazon Bedrock, Amazon Neptune, and personalized PageRank
all_items.summary: In this post, we demonstrate how to implement HippoRAG using a comprehensive AWS stack. We use Amazon Bedrock for LLM capabilities, Amazon Neptune for graph database functionality, Amazon Neptune Analytics for advanced graph algorithms including Personalized PageRank, and Amazon Titan Embeddings for vector representations. This implementation showcases how to build and deploy HippoRAG within AWS infrastructure for enterprise-scale applications.

all_items.title: How Inscribe uses Amazon Bedrock to stop document fraud in seconds
all_items.summary: In this post, you will learn how Inscribe developed an agentic AI system using Amazon Bedrock that reasons across documents the way an expert fraud analyst would. With this new agentic AI system, Inscribe now detects tampered, fabricated, and AI-generated financial documents in under 90 seconds. This is a 20x improvement over traditional manual review, while maintaining the accuracy and explainability required by financial services regulations.

all_items.title: Simplify model selection in Amazon Bedrock with the open source Model Profiler
all_items.summary: The Amazon Bedrock Model Profiler is an open source tool that aggregates model metadata from multiple AWS APIs and external sources into a single, searchable interface. In this post, you’ll learn what the Model Profiler provides, the real-world scenarios it supports, and how to deploy it in your own environment in under five minutes.

all_items.title: Accelerate protein design with BoltzGen on Amazon SageMaker AI
all_items.summary: In this post, we demonstrate how to deploy BoltzGen on SageMaker AI and run an end-to-end protein design experiment. By the end of the walkthrough, you have a working setup that scales from quick validation runs to production batch processing. The setup offers two execution modes for different stages of research and uses step-level caching to reduce compute expenses during iterative workflows.
